It is hoped that increased efforts will be made amongst the strong-holds of Cholera, so that the disease may cease to be the dreadful scourge it has proved in the past. Our only effectual safety lies in the disease ceasing to exist in Egypt. The last volume of the Census Returns has just been issued. I have examined these Returns, and have extracted those Tables which referred to the Whitechapel District. I have prefaced this Report with them, so that they might be readily available for future reference. As. these figures are open to inspection by any requiring special information, I shall only revert to the altered condition since the last Census from one point of view, viz:�the influence of Foreign immigration, upon the Whitechapel District. Included in the City of London, Shoreditch, Bethnal Green, Stepney, St. George-in-the-East, Mile End Old Town and Poplar, 39,307 foreigners of all nationalities were present on the Census night, and of these, Whitechapel possessed 17,961. Taking, however, only Russians and Russian Poles, the Whitechapel District possesses 13,538, of these country people as compared with 10,213 distributed amongst all the other East End Parishes, including the City of London.

No re-vaccinated person properly so called contracted the disease. A second letter as to persons who had Small-pox, and who were not removed to hospital, was received from the Local Government Board. The matters mentioned therein have been included in the above Report. I have only to add that I have supplied the Infirmary Medical Superintendent with Vaccine Lymph sufficient to re-vaccinate the staff and many of the patients. So far as I can learn, only one woman�a scrubber at the Infirmarycontracted Small-pox. She had not been re-vaccinated. I believe that I have re-vaccinated nearly all the persons who are employed at the Salvation Army Shelter in the Whitechapel Road, and also the men employed at the Victoria Home, No. 1 in Commercial Street, where 8 of the cases occurred. As a matter of fact, therefore, 50 per cent, of the cases were reported as coming from Salvation Army Shelters, 25 per cent, from private houses, and 25 per cent, from Registered Common Lodging-houses, the Whitechapel Infirmary, and from all outside Philanthropic Shelters. At present about 16 of the cases may be centres from which fresh cases may arise, and to these our attention must remain for the present directed.

Probably, early in the Session, some legislation will take place to exehange for some of the present regulations, others of a less drastic kind. In the meantime I would warn persons who wish to be protected from so awful a disease as Small-pox, to inquire into the advantages of vaccination for themselves, and not to believe persons who, for other reasons than those of public policy, make statements which are often altogether at variance with truth. * Page 28. 8 I am somewhat handicapped in this matter, because I am officially conconcerned with vaccination�and I have been accused of supporting it for interested purposes. It does not appear to occur to these people that the Medical Profession lose vastly by anything which tends towards the entire removal of any disease. I am looking at two large posters which have been largely circulated throughout the Hamlet of Mile End Old Town and the Whitechapel District. The latter states that "the Guardians of the White"chapel Union will not prosecute vaccination defaulters. On Tuesday, "December 14th, 1897, the Guardians decided to suspend prosecutions. "Therefore ignore all notices that threaten prosecution in 14 days." I am informed by the Clerk to the Board of Guardians for Whitechapel that this statement is absolutely untrue.
